clue.text: Noble champion?

definitions.meaning: a noble such as a duke or earl holds a hereditary rank of nobility
the reigning champion in a sport holds the championship belt or crown

explanation.surface: A question about whether an aristocrat could also be a sporting winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a peer with a rank and a sporting champion possess a named distinction, one inherited and one won.

clue.text: Movement in broadcast millions missed

indicators.note: missed tells us the letter for millions is left out of the broadcast word

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to transmit it
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A broadcast that skipped the millions watching a movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage or conveyance from one place to another, a kind of movement.

clue.text: Beginning of traditional ceremony, lacking originality

indicators.note: the beginning of the word traditional is just its opening letter

parts.note: a rite is a solemn ceremony

explanation.surface: The start of a time-honoured ceremony judged unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hackneyed and stale through overuse lacks any originality.

clue.text: High point of achievement of the first lady and others

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible, the first lady in a literal sense
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: The peak of success reached by a First Lady and her companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but here she is the biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's tallest mountain is used figuratively for the ultimate peak of any endeavour.

clue.text: Taking vacation, small number lacking energy to go to desert

indicators.note: lacking says the letter for energy is dropped from the number

parts.note: one is a small number
E is the physics symbol for energy
to desert someone is to leave them

explanation.surface: A tired soldier on holiday, out of energy, heading for the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go to' simply joins the pieces; 'desert' is a verb, not sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away from work or duty on a holiday is being on leave.

clue.text: One opposing official policy — leader of Democrats insisted upon change

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Democrats
change tells us to rearrange the letters of insisted

explanation.surface: A rebel against party policy as the Democrats' leader demands reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon' is only a link; 'change' is the anagram signal, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident is a person who openly disagrees with an established government or doctrine.

clue.text: All are staggering having consumed English booze

indicators.note: having consumed means the scrambled letters swallow another piece
staggering drunkenly suggests the letters of all are reeling about

explanation.surface: Drinkers stagger after downing English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' rearranges ALL ARE into RALALE, and E for English goes inside after the R. Real ale is a British term for traditional cask-conditioned beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned traditional beer is a kind of alcoholic drink, informally booze.

clue.text: Conjecture in East about 'Wise Men'

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the first letters wrap the wise men

parts.note: taken as written
the Magi are the Wise Men of the Nativity story

explanation.surface: Speculation about the Wise Men coming from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjecture is to guess or suppose, as to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Girl tethers barking dog

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of tethers go wild

explanation.surface: A girl ties up a dog that is barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' seems to describe the dog but is British slang for crazy, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter from Ireland is a breed of gundog.

clue.text: Callas working on aria's ending in opera house

indicators.note: working implies the letters of Callas are put to work in a new order
the ending of aria's is its final letter

explanation.surface: The soprano Maria Callas perfecting an aria in a famous theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Milan theatre is one of the world's most celebrated venues for opera.

clue.text: Defoliant spy ring dropped on field

parts.note: an agent is a spy
O is shaped like a ring
a range is an area of open land or a field of operation

explanation.surface: A spy ring parachuted onto a field with a chemical weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The herbicide used by the US in Vietnam stripped leaves from jungle trees.

clue.text: Paper having no time for children

indicators.note: having no time means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper too busy to cover children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like the definition, a newspaper edition, but supplies the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal and formal usage one's offspring are referred to collectively by this word.

clue.text: Get rid of last of cattle spread out round Cape

indicators.note: the last of cattle is its final letter
round means the spreading word goes around the cape letter

parts.note: to radiate is to spread out from a centre
C is the map abbreviation for Cape

explanation.surface: Wiping out the remaining cattle scattered around a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread out' looks like an anagram signal but is the synonym RADIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely or remove utterly.

clue.text: Latest to pick out popular nightclub?

parts.note: hot news is the latest news
to spot something is to pick it out

explanation.surface: Identifying the trendiest club in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, fashionable venue where crowds gather is a hotspot; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Border safe? Gulf ruler turns up, being welcomed in

indicators.note: being welcomed in means the ruler's letters go inside the safe

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the ruler's letters are read upwards

parts.note: an emir is a ruler in the Persian Gulf states

explanation.surface: A ruler from the Gulf arrives at a frontier and is welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' for a safe is old British underworld slang; 'turns up' reads the ruler upwards in this down clue before 'being welcomed in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter is the outer edge or boundary of an area.

clue.text: As an example, copper piece

definitions.meaning: copper is one example of a chemical substance in the periodic table
a piece or component of a larger whole

explanation.surface: Using a copper coin as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a chemical element, and an element is also a constituent part of something.

clue.text: Trade ban: almost board ship and depart

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is lost

parts.note: to embark is to board a ship
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: A trade embargo means travellers barely board before the ship leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition on commerce with a country.

clue.text: Marilyn Monroe film kiss — high point

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
the top is the highest point

explanation.surface: A screen kiss as the climax of a Monroe movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1956 comedy starring Marilyn Monroe shares its title with a roadside halt for buses.

clue.text: Office item available with mounted pictures going over year

parts.note: a product that is out has been released and is available

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pictures word climbs upward

parts.note: art means pictures

explanation.surface: Framed office pictures on hand for another year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns the pictures upward in this down clue; 'going over' just sets them above the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray on a desk for finished correspondence and papers is a piece of office equipment.

clue.text: Whole unit, say, brought into Bury?

indicators.note: brought into means the example letters are put inside the burial word

parts.note: to inter is to bury; the question mark warns it is not the Lancashire town
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A whole unit brought into the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number such as one, with no fractional part, is what mathematicians call it.

clue.text: Animal smell, not pleasant, over area in pub

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the smell above the area letter

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A beast's foul stench in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means brutish and lacking human feeling, cruel and savage.

clue.text: Slow guard, out of position by a lake

indicators.note: out of position tells us the letters of guard are misplaced

explanation.surface: A sluggish sentry has strayed from his post beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual describes something happening slowly, by degrees.

clue.text: International striker on trial

indicators.note: on places the striker after the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A footballer on trial for a national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests football, but it is a match. A test match is an international game of cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a game between national teams, so an international fixture.

clue.text: Mark's short visit home

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a stay is a visit
in means at home

explanation.surface: A brief visit home leaves a trace.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish or discoloured spot is a mark.

clue.text: Small and friendly crowd

parts.note: warm means friendly

explanation.surface: A small, welcoming gathering of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large dense moving mass, of insects or people.

clue.text: Muscle seen from both sides

indicators.note: seen from both sides hints that the word reads alike in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A muscle viewed from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotator cuff muscles turn the shoulder, and a rotator is a muscle that rotates a limb.

clue.text: Maine, a certain size

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A particular dimension in the state of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Size and measure both mean the extent or dimensions of something.

clue.text: Good-time girl from Malaya? Print blurred

indicators.note: blurred print is jumbled and unclear, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smudged photograph of a fun-loving woman from Malaya.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves socialising and revelry, a pleasure-seeker, is described with this informal phrase.
